full_judgment:
4. The plaintiff case, in short, are that Father of the plaintiff, late Faiz Ahmed divorced his first wife Selima Ahmed, mother of the plaintiff in 1984 when he was 2 (two) years old, then he obtained the guardianship and custodian of the plaintiff through court; that thereafter his father took Helena Khatun, defendant No. 1 as second wife in the year 1988 and through his second wife defendant Nos. 2-3 was born; that the plaintiffs father died on 27-12-2013 after long suffering from chronic disease for long 2 years; that at the time of death he left plaintiff as one son by first wife, second wife, Helena Faiz, daughter Farhin Faiz, son Tanjim Faiz by second wife; that plaintiff owing to his job staying at Canada due to which he appointed his maternal uncle, Mr Alhaj Khondakar Musle Uddin as his attorney on 17-4-2014; that the father of the plaintiff got allotment a plot of land measuring an area of 7.104 decimal of from Government Housing Settlement Department, now under National Housing Authority (shortly, NHA) at Mirpur Road No. 1, Block-B, section-1, being commercial plot building No. 6/A, same was allotted to him by allotment letter dated 07.07.1981 and said plot of 'Ka' schedule land was delivered to him physically; that thereafter Housing Settlement Department executed registered lease agreement being Lease Deed No. 2214 dated 10-6-1982, accordingly his name was recorded in the city Jarip by filing Mutation Case No. 127-47(S)/82 dated 21-10-1982; that father of the plaintiff constructed 8 storied building by approval of the plan from RAJUK; that his father inherited 1570 sft of flat of 7th floor of 9 storied building known as "Tower Hamlet", situated in "Kha" schedule land of plot No. 4/8, Block- F under Lalmatia Housing Estate which was developed by a Developer Company, after his demise, the said property should be partitioned amongst his heirs; that the plaintiff after coming back to Bangladesh on 6-3-2014 came to know that the defendants in collusion with each other made a sale deed No.12061 dated 15-10-2012 in respect of 3rd and 4th floor against minimum consideration of money which is a forged deed and another transfer deed No. 10400 dated 23-9-2013 which was got by defendant Nos. 9 and 10 due to which they have submitted an amended deed No. 2903 dated 12-3-2014 and 13-3-2014; thereafter the attorney of the plaintiff in response to the request of defendant No. 1 sat together on 24-4-2014 for amicable settlement, he informed that no money was left in the account; that the Fourth floor of 'ka' schedule building is transferred to defendant Nos. 4-6 and rest 4 floors were distributed equally by Faiz Ahmed to his heirs by executing Wasiatnama; that the attorney of the plaintiff by obtaining the certified copy found that all deeds are found to be irregular and unethical and consideration money were not properly shown and further found that defendant No. 7 being a brother of defendant No. 1 manipulated everything to manufacture sale deeds and Wasiatnama without obtaining any consent from the plaintiff's father; that it further appears that the plaintiff's father died on 27-12-2013 and Wasiatnama deed is shown to be executed two months before his death; that the plaintiff inherited 35% share in all schedule properties and money; that defendant Nos. 1-3 by taking the advantage of joint account with the father of the plaintiff they have withdrawn the money according to their sweet will and spoiled the money and at last on 30-4-2014 the plaintiff through his attorney gave a proposal to settle amicably for partitioning the properties but the defendant refused to do so. 

 6. Defendant Nos. 4-6 filed written objection on 27-4-2016 and Defendant No. 1 also contested the injunction application by filing separate written objection on 3-5-2016. That the case of the defendant Nos. 1, 4-6 are that father of the plaintiff during his lifetime executed bainanama with the defendant Nos. 4-6 for sale of 1st, 2nd and 3rd floor more or less 12,000 sft as specifically mentioned in schedule 'Ica' to the plaint for a total consideration of Taka 4,60,00,000 out of which Taka 30,00,000 was paid as advanced and bainanama was registered being No. 15083 dated 13-12-2011. It was further stated that the plaintiff during his lifetime filed an application for sale permission before the Lessor National Housing Authority-defendant No. 9 to transfer the properties mentioned in the bainanama and defendant Nos. 9-10 accordingly issued sale permission dated 11-10-2012 in favour of the lessee, Faiz Ahmed. Subsequently, predecessor of the plaintiff, Faiz Ahmed executed two sale deeds being registered sale deed Nos. 12060 dated 15-10-2012 showing transfer of 3rd and 4th floor measuring 3,075 sft. and another sale deed being No. 10400 dated 23-9-2013 showing transfer of Ground and 2nd floor each for an area of 3075 sft. Then the defendant Nos.4-6 filed an application before the office of defendant Nos. 9-10 for mutating their names by memo dated 28-4-2016. It may be noted that Faiz Ahmed, the original allottee/lessee of the suit schedule 'ka' and `kha' property died on 27-12-2013. 

 10. Mr Kamal-ul-Alam, the learned Advocate with Mr JK Paul, Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-appellant. Mr Kamal-ul-Alam, the learned Advocate at the very outset submits that the National Housing Authority mutated the names of the defendant Nos. 4-6 during subsistence   of the order of injunction against them. He further submits that the trial court was wrong in law in finding that the plaintiff did not specify his share in the schedule land and, as such, he is not entitled to get an order of injunction. He further submits that the trial court did not at all consider the specific allegation of the plaintiff that the alleged acquisition of right and title of the defendants on the basis of Wasiatnama and the sale deeds are tamed with fraud. He next submits that the trial court was wrong in law in holding that section 134 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act barred the jurisdiction of the civil court with regard to mutation. He categorically submits that the said section has no manner of application in the case of mutation by the National Housing Authority with regard to leasehold land owned by it. He finally submits that the petitioner did not seek any injunction against the National Housing Authority but sought injunction against the defendant Nos. 4-6 from mutating their names in the office of National Housing Authority. In support of his submissions learned Advocate has cited the following decisions namely 14 MLR (AD) 111 and 24 BLD (AD) 282 = 9 BLC (AD) 272.
